  1. Amber draws two different cumulative frequency graphs. These are shown below. Which of the two should she use to represent her data? Explain your reasoning.

Graph A:

Graph B:

  1. Amber shows the correct graph to Terry who says that it shows that week on week her sales are increasing. With reference to the graph, explain whether Terry is correct.

  2. Terry goes on to say that Amber can use the correct graph to estimate the exact time during a week that Amber had sold half of the ice creams. Explain why this would be inappropriate.
steps:
a)

Graph B should be used as the data should be plotted at the top end of each class interval.

b)

The data is cumulative, so an increasing gradient would show that sales week on week are increasing. However, at the end of the 5th week, the gradient starts to decrease and so the number of sales here are decreasing.

c)

Amber only sold ice creams on a Sunday. Estimating from the graph would assume that the sales of ice creams were evenly spread across the week, which is not the case.
